items.text: hardcoded database name without env override
items.reason: Database names are read from the environment with literals only as local defaults (`process.env.TEST_DATABASE ?? 'test_migrations'`), and Testcontainers supplies the URL programmatically.

items.text: testing constraints at the ORM level only
items.reason: The document explicitly directs constraint assertions to the `pool.query` level, not the ORM or application-validation layer, which it says can mask a missing DB constraint.
Shared state is listed as Anti-Pattern #2 and the document prescribes transaction rollback or per-test cleanup for isolation.

items.text: assume rollback is possible without testing
items.reason: The document mandates forward AND backward migration tests and provides a runnable rollback test using down.sql.
Using `prisma db push` / `synchronize: true` instead of real migrations is listed as Anti-Pattern #5 and warned against.
Timing uses EXPLAIN ANALYZE Execution Time and `performance.now()`; no waitForTimeout appears anywhere.
The data-preservation test inserts a user row before applying the migration under test.
The preservation test asserts the inserted email survives and the new nullable column is null.

items.text: no NULL check in WHERE clause
items.reason: Orphan-detection anti-joins include `WHERE u.id IS NULL` / `WHERE o.id IS NULL` checks, and null-count audits are included.
Testing only happy-path queries is listed as Anti-Pattern #6; constraint-rejection and empty-result tests are required.
The document runs explicit orphan-record anti-join queries and foreign_key_check pragmas rather than assuming integrity.
